results.title: Devt of advanced early warning system for quake underway
results.description: SANTA ANA, Cagayan — A foreign disaster response expert, Indonesia Deputy Minister Abdul Muhari of Badan Nasional Penanggulangan Bencana (Indonesian National Disaster Management Agency), reported on Thursday about a worldwide action to develop advanced early warning systems for preparedness. Speaking after the 4th Quarter Nationwide Simultaneous Earthquake Drill (NSED) at the coastline of this town, Muhari said "Disaster risk management must connect scientific knowledge and community behavior (so) everyone must play an active role in strengthening tsunami preparedness and protecting lives from tsunami threats." He added that while this should not be the case, they are trying to develop more advanced early warning systems so more vulnerable people can access it. Muhari said that public trust is important in mitigating tsunami impacts and "constructed emergency response buildings must be both accessible and trusted by the community." “One of the reasons for this was that even when facilities such as vertical evacuation centers are theoretically effective, it does not guarantee that people will use it. Sometimes... safety means where most people go," he said. Muhari also said that people must be able to make decisions based on natural signs in case of telecommunication failures. "The system is there but the community should not solely depend on the system," the deputy minister said. He reminded listeners that local knowledge must be connected to scientific knowledge which in turn becomes public policy that translates into practical solutions. Civil Defense Administrator Undersecretary Harold Cabreros has called on the public to strengthen tsunami preparedness amid the risks faced by coastal communities as government agencies and partners observed World Tsunami Awareness Day (WTAD) on Thursday. The activity was in support of the United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR) campaign anchored on the theme "Be Tsunami Ready: Resilience Starts with You." The campaign emphasized that building resilient communities begins with individual awareness, preparedness, and collective action. Civil defense officials and science experts have cited general preparedness of local executives and disaster responders during the drill. Drill evaluators during the event lauded participants for their "efficiency, public discipline, and operational readiness" that made the exercises successful, civil defense organizers said. The evaluators cited the drill organizers during the alarm and response phase, evacuation and movement, assembly and headcount at the higher ground for the tsunami drill, and leadership during the disaster control and command. The OCD said the drill is aligned with the preparation against the "very strong El Niño," which is being felt in the tropical Pacific and is expected to persist until the first half of 2027, potentially reaching its peak by the end of 2026. During the forum, weather and disaster response officials cited that El Niño increases the likelihood of rainfall deficits, "which may result in dry spells and drought in several areas of the country." “However, above-normal rainfall conditions may still occur due to the passage of tropical cyclones and other rain-bearing weather systems,” the experts said. In a latest drought assessment by the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa), 11 provinces were under dry spell, and 10 provinces experienced dry conditions in October 2026.
creator: vince jacob visaya
